items.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Right. You said about horn players it makes me think of Louis Hayes said something about he watched Cannonball and Nat’s rear ends for years. [INTERVIEWEE] Right, right, right, right.

ctx.x: Right. I mean it’s always an ear thing. I mean I don’t have to see anybody. It’s great to be able to see the leader especially because obviously there’s cues and little things that you may notice. That’s important. But as far as seeing all the musicians while they’re playing I mean the one player that stands out front, for the most part they don’t see anybody. So you don’t really have to see the person, but in the rhythm section sometimes eye contact is really great. So if you’re not really having the best…
Right. You said about horn players it makes me think of Louis Hayes said something about he watched Cannonball and Nat’s rear ends for years.
